X1 has a meaningful positive effect on Y1 (OAT range=0.24) and a small positive effect on Y4 (OAT=0.058) — both were predicted flat.
X5 has NO effect on Y4 (exactly 0.0) — I predicted a small decrease based on initial correlation of -0.17.

new_findings: X6 has a MAJOR nonlinear positive effect on Y1 at high X2: Y1 increased from 0.948 to 1.132 (new maximum!) when X6 went from 0.1 to 1.0 at X2=1.0. The local gradient at X6=0.1 was −0.033, completely misleading about the full-range effect.
X6 reduces Y2 at high X2 levels: at X2=1.0, Y2 dropped from 0.362 to 0.303 as X6 went from 0.1 to 1.0, while Y1 simultaneously increased dramatically.
The X6 dimension creates a second trade-off axis on the Pareto front: at high X2, increasing X6 trades Y4 (decreases from 0.322 to 0.249) for much higher Y1 and lower Y2.
X5 saturates extremely quickly: going from X5=0.5 to X5=1.0 at X2=0.5 only improved Y1 by 0.003, far less than gradient-predicted 0.036.
Extended the Pareto front to 17+ points across two dimensions (X2 and X6), achieving hypervolume improvement from 0.2425 to >0.28.
At X2=0.8–0.9 with X6=1.0, we get Y1≈0.95–1.04 at Y2≈0.27–0.29 — points that dramatically outperform the X6=0.1 frontier in Y1 at similar Y2.
surprises: The gradient dY1/dX6 = −0.033 at [1,1,1,1,1,0.1] predicted X6 slightly hurts Y1, but the actual effect of X6=0.1→1.0 was +0.184 on Y1. The X6→Y1 function has a local minimum near X6=0.1 then rises sharply — finite-difference gradients at boundaries can be catastrophically misleading for nonlinear functions.
Y1 predictions for X6 sweep were systematically 0.07–0.21 too low — the nonlinear X6 acceleration was much stronger than any linear extrapolation suggested.

X5 'free improvement' was 10x smaller than expected (0.003 vs 0.036 predicted from gradient). The saturation is extremely sharp — the gradient at X5=0.5 (0.073) massively overstates the remaining gain.
The X2×X6 interaction on Y2 is dramatic: dY2/dX6 = +0.169 at X2=0.3 but −0.147 at X2=1.0. This sign reversal was not anticipated from early exploration.
